record.noComponentModified: Verified after the batch: 13 component sets re-read and matched on name, variant count and property count — Autocomplete/Field 30, Autocomplete/Option 5, Autocomplete/Tag 2, Text field 20, Checkbox 24, Menu 2, Menu/Item 6, Button group/Segment 54, Button 72, Split button 8, Table/Cell 6, Table/Row 3, Paper 12. record.pageLayoutIntact: All seven Compositions-page section x/y positions are byte-identical to the start of the batch; sections grew in HEIGHT only. Zero section overlaps. Frames were repositioned only WITHIN their own section, preserving production-count order: Autocomplete (88 files) above Select + Menu (74) in Inputs; Button group segment row (20) above Selection / bulk action bar (14) in Actions. Data display frame positions were left exactly as hand-placed.

recurringAcrossCompositions.oneTextPropertyPerRow: Autocomplete/Option, Menu/Item and Table/Cell each expose exactly one TEXT property, and in all three production overwhelmingly needs more — 52 of 88 Autocomplete files customise the option row, 57 of 230 MenuItems need icon/two-line/checkbox/spinner content, and 87 of 164 table cells hold a component. This is one component-layer problem showing up three times, not three composition problems.
recurringAcrossCompositions.instancesCannotHostChildren: The same Figma constraint forced scaffolding in three frames: the Autocomplete listbox cannot be a Paper instance, a Menu cannot exceed its four slots, and a Table/Row cannot take real cells. It is the single largest driver of drawn-rather-instanced nodes across the batch.
recurringAcrossCompositions.stateVersusContent: Table/Row and Button group/Segment share a shape: the component that owns the visual states cannot carry the content production needs, so the states go unused. Table/Row is used in 1 of 12 sections; Button group/Segment has no selected state at all.
recurringAcrossCompositions.outlinedIsUnstyled: ButtonGroupOverrides styles only contained keys, leaving 4 outlined groups with MUI stock appearance — the SAME shape as the alert composition's finding that AlertOverrides has no outlined rules. Worth treating as a theme-layer pattern rather than two isolated bugs.
recurringAcrossCompositions.productionOverridesTheThemeDefault: Three independent cases: 24 of 25 Autocomplete files override noOptionsText; 12 of 23 ButtonGroups override the library colour default back to MUI's; 53 of 106 Autocompletes decline the size the theme does not set. Where the theme takes a position, production frequently takes another.

record.instanceRatioMethodNote: The build prompt cites dialog 87.5% and alert 92%. Those figures could NOT be reproduced by any measure applied here. Measured identically across all frames: all-authored-nodes gives Autocomplete 18.9%, Select+Menu 17.1%, Segment row 21.6%, Table 41.6%, against alert 11.6% and dialog 15.1%; excluding annotation text gives 35.1 / 34.9 / 41.7 / 53.8 against alert 21.3 and dialog 35.9; a UI-elements-only heuristic gives 55.1 for Autocomplete against alert 63.9 and dialog 60.9. On every consistent measure all four new frames sit at or above the two templates. The 87.5/92 baseline should be treated as unreliable until its method is recorded.
record.toolingBuilt: composition-scan.js (balanced-brace JSX scanner with import-source resolution and TSX generic handling) and comp-analyze.js, in C:/Code/design system. Reusable for the remaining compositions.
record.constraintHit: Node deletion was blocked by the harness for the whole batch, so every frame was brought up to template additively — mutating text in place and reparenting accurate content rather than removing anything. This suited the prompt's delete-nothing rule, and no content was lost; the only cost was one stray empty text node in the segment row, which was repurposed into a real note rather than removed.
